_comment: Everything the container needs in order to offer, fetch and install a toolchain.
The dashboard's Library renders it and `aerie toolchains` acts on it; adding a toolchain
here is the whole job, as long as it fits one of the five kinds below.
name     what `aerie toolchains install|remove` is called with.
probe    where it lands, so the page can tell installed from not: a bare
name is a directory under the toolchain store root, android:<pkg> a package
directory under ANDROID_HOME. System images are not toolchains;
they have a section of their own, above.
platforms  which <os>/<arch> this recipe actually works on. Seven of these
name linux-x86_64 in their URL, and swift names ubuntu24.04, so
"Linux" is not one platform here. `*` in the arch position means
the payload is arch-independent: shell and jars, a git clone, or
a tool that resolves its own platform. An install onto a node
outside the list is refused by name rather than downloading a
couple of hundred megabytes and failing on exec.
requires   other toolchains this one needs in order to work. Installed
first, and only when missing. android-tools drives sdkmanager,
which is a Java program, and without this it failed inside
sdkmanager with a message naming neither Java nor the toolchain
that supplies it.
layout     where this toolchain lands, once, for everybody who needs to
know. `bin` are directories under it to put on PATH, `env` the
variables it sets (valued as a path under it, or =VALUE for a value, "" meaning the
toolchain directory itself), `tool` the file whose presence
proves it is installed, and `reports` the name the census
summary calls it. Written here because it was written in four
places (sdk_env_snippet, the agent's STORE_TOOLS and
STORE_PATHS, and sdk_check_one) and they drifted three times
in one day.
A path may start `root:` to mean relative to the store rather
than to this toolchain; the android toolchains share one tree,
since sdkmanager installs into <root>/android whatever the
package is called.
system   the machine's own packages this one needs at runtime, by
package manager: `apt` for the Debian family. A recipe runs
as the job account, so the AGENT installs these first, as
root, on a node it may administer (a managed one); on any
other it names them and carries on, and the tool says which
are missing when it is used. Playwright's browsers are the
case: forty libraries the image gets from install-deps and a
node got from nowhere. An entry may name alternatives,
"libasound2t64|libasound2": a library renamed between
releases, met by whichever is installed and otherwise the
first the machine's repositories carry, since apt refuses a
whole install for one unknown name. tools/check-sysdeps.py
checks every name against each release's package index.
source   how to get it. {dir} is the install directory, {version} whatever
the version resolver returned, {script} a downloaded installer.
kind: tarball      resolve a version, fetch source.url, unpack with strip.
script       fetch source.url and run it with the given args and env.
git          shallow-clone a branch; the tool then updates in place.
command      run something already in the image, pointed at {dir}.
sdkmanager   an android package, installed by sdkmanager.
fresh_only   refuse when the directory already exists, for the recipes that
unpack rather than merge.
verify       run after installing, so a broken unpack fails the install
rather than waiting to fail the first time somebody uses it.
time upstream ships: what a toolchain weighs is measured from the disk once it
is installed, remembered after it is removed, and read from the download's
own Content-Length before that when the URL is the payload itself.
download   how to find out what an install would fetch, for a row that is
not installed yet. Absent means source.url is the payload and
its Content-Length is the answer; "command-urls" runs a dry run
and matches the URLs out of it, which is how playwright's five
bundles and the .NET archive are counted. A recipe that cannot
and the row shows no size until it has been installed once.
No size is written down here. One typed into a file is wrong the next time
upstream ships: a row shows what the toolchain takes on this disk once it is
installed, what it took the last time it was, or what the download weighs
before that. Never a number somebody guessed.
"url-matches" fetches a file upstream publishes and matches the
URLs out of it, which is how rust's three minimal-profile
components are counted; "android-repo" reads sdkmanager's own
index, keyed by the package id an install resolves to; and
"approximate" is a number written down, for the one recipe whose
download cannot be measured before it happens: a git clone has
no content length. It is marked as an approximation everywhere
it is shown.
terms: what installing it is under, each {label, url}, with accept: true for an agreement installing accepts (Google's, NVIDIA's, Apple's) rather than an open-source license. Drawn on the row.

maker: who the tool is by, an organization or a person, drawn on its card beside the tier; a toolchain that carries several makers' tools is by AerieOS and names each under credits, [{name, maker}], which its Details page lists.
checksum (R137) where the publisher states what a tarball's or script's download is,
checked before it is unpacked or run (sdkmeta.py checksum): github-asset,
file (url template), go-json, zig-index, json (url, path), android-repo,
zsync, signature (sig, keys: a detached signature checked with config/release-keys),
or none with why; a file source may be signed (signed: sig, keys).
Each of those asks the file's own origin at the moment of the install. A pin does
not: {from: pin, version, sha256} carries the version and the sha256 of the exact
file (one digest, or one per platform keyed as source.url is), so the row itself
says what the download is. A pinned row installs that version with nobody asked,
and source.version stays as how a newer one is found.
fetch    what the install downloads besides its own source, declared: each {url, to} with
the sha256 it is held to, or signed: {sig, keys} where its publisher's detached
signature holds it, and platform where it is for one <os>/<arch>. AerieOS fetches
and checks each into the directory before anything of the row runs (sdk.sh
sdk_declared), and what runs then (a script's installer, a command, the then
steps, a warm-up, the verify) runs with no network. A row whose own download is a
pin, or is held by its publisher's signature (signature, or file with signed), is
cut the same way by that alone; offline: true says it of a command or a repository
that downloads nothing more.
online   one sentence, for a row whose installer downloads the rest by itself: what, and
from where. Its declared downloads are fetched and checked all the same, and its
steps keep the network; the install, its receipt and its row say the sentence.
keyring  {name: an armored public key}: a publisher's keys the row carries itself, which a
signature's keys names and which wins over config/release-keys' file of that name.
How a newer pin is found is in the row too, for the tool that proposes one (tools/pins.py: check,
move, pin, verify) and for no install, which takes the pin and asks nobody:
version  (source.version) the resolver that finds the newest version: text, match (url, match:
a document and a pattern whose first group is the version), github-release (repo; or
with tag, settled and asset the newest release whose tag matches, out that many days,
and the file in it whose name matches, per platform), node-index, zig-index. One that
supplies the address itself has the tool write source.url beside the digest.
found    (checksum.found, of a pin) how the new file's digest is learned from its publisher's
statement without downloading it, written as a checksum that asks the origin is.
Where the publisher states no sha256 the tool downloads the file and hashes it.
a declared download may say version (fills {version} in its url and its signature's, never in
to), track (how a newer one is found, as source.version is written) and found.
commit, tag, track  (a git source) the commit the clone is fetched at, the tag fetched by name
beside it and kept only where it is at that commit, and how the commit to pin is
found: {resolver: git-tag, match} the newest tag matching, {resolver: git-branch,
branch} a branch's head. With branch the checkout is called it and follows its origin.
A download with no version in its address has nothing to track: it is pinned by its digest and
refused when its vendor changes it, until the pin moves.
System images, which are not toolchains. A toolchain is one thing at one
version; a system image exists at every API level at once, and which of
them you want is a question about what you are testing, not about the
catalog. So the flavors live here as data, and the Emulator tab offers an
API level and a flavor rather than a row per flavor that could only
ever install the newest one.
abi      the only one an x86_64 host can run at any speed.
xml      sdkmanager's own index for that flavor: what levels exist,
and what each weighs before it is downloaded.
about    which one to pick, which is the whole question.

google_apis.label: Google APIs
google_apis.about: Google Play services (Maps, sign-in, push) but no Play Store app. Rootable: `adb root` works, which the Play Store images refuse. This is the default, and what aerie emu create fetches.

google_apis_playstore.label: Google APIs + Play Store
google_apis_playstore.about: The same, plus the Play Store app itself, for anything that has to sign in to Play, check a license or take an in-app payment. A Play-certified build, so it is not rootable. Google ships it as a separate image; there is no image that is one plus a switch.

android-wear.label: Wear OS
android-wear.about: What modern Galaxy and Pixel watches run. Round screen, tiny API level numbers of its own.

toolchains.name: jdk
toolchains.label: JDK 21 (Temurin)
toolchains.about: Java 21, which Gradle, sdkmanager and the emulator tools need. The first thing a node needs for Android work.

toolchains.name: android-tools
toolchains.label: Android command-line tools
toolchains.about: sdkmanager and avdmanager, through which every other Android toolchain installs. Sets this node's ANDROID_HOME.

run: { command -v unzip >/dev/null 2>&1 && unzip -q "$1" -d "$2"; } || python3 -c "import os,sys,zipfile;z=zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]);[(z.extract(i,sys.argv[2]), (i.external_attr>>16) and os.chmod(os.path.join(sys.argv[2],i.filename), i.external_attr>>16)) for i in z.infolist()]" "$1" "$2" && root="$(dirname "$2")/android" && mkdir -p "$root/cmdline-tools" && rm -rf "$root/cmdline-tools/latest" && ln -sfn "$2/cmdline-tools" "$root/cmdline-tools/latest"
after: system images and the emulator install through it: aerie toolchains install android:emulator, aerie emu image add ID

toolchains.name: android:cmake
toolchains.label: Android CMake
toolchains.about: The CMake the NDK's build system uses.

source.online: sdkmanager, the program of the Android command-line tools, downloads this package from dl.google.com by itself and holds it to the sha1 Google's repository listing states.

toolchains.name: android:emulator
toolchains.label: Android emulator
toolchains.about: The Android emulator. Its system images, one per API level, are added on the Emulator tab. Google ships it for x86_64 Linux only.

source.online: sdkmanager, the program of the Android command-line tools, downloads this package from dl.google.com by itself and holds it to the sha1 Google's repository listing states.

toolchains.name: android:platform-tools
toolchains.label: Android platform tools
toolchains.about: adb and the other tools that talk to a phone or an emulator; the emulator and the Phone tab need it. Google ships it for x86_64 Linux only.

source.online: sdkmanager, the program of the Android command-line tools, downloads this package from dl.google.com by itself and holds it to the sha1 Google's repository listing states.

toolchains.name: android:platforms
toolchains.label: Android SDK Platform (newest level)
toolchains.about: The android.jar a build compiles against (compileSdk), at the newest level Google publishes. Update adds the next level beside it, so older projects keep building. Removing this removes every level.

source.online: sdkmanager, the program of the Android command-line tools, downloads this package from dl.google.com by itself and holds it to the sha1 Google's repository listing states.

toolchains.name: android:build-tools
toolchains.label: Android SDK Build-Tools (newest)
toolchains.about: aapt2, d8, zipalign and apksigner at the newest stable version. Update adds the next beside it.

source.online: sdkmanager, the program of the Android command-line tools, downloads this package from dl.google.com by itself and holds it to the sha1 Google's repository listing states.

toolchains.name: android:ndk
toolchains.label: Android NDK
toolchains.about: Native development kit, for C and C++ inside an Android app.

source.online: sdkmanager, the program of the Android command-line tools, downloads this package from dl.google.com by itself and holds it to the sha1 Google's repository listing states.

toolchains.name: flutter
toolchains.label: Flutter
toolchains.about: Flutter with its Dart SDK. Builds Android apps on Linux, and iOS too on a Mac with Xcode.

source.warm_note: warming the toolchain (downloads the bundled dart sdk)
source.online: Its first run downloads the Dart SDK and the engine's artifacts for this machine from storage.googleapis.com, and its own tool's packages from pub.dev.

toolchains.name: go
toolchains.label: Go
toolchains.about: Go, which cross-compiles to Windows, macOS, Linux and ARM with nothing else to install.

toolchains.name: dotnet
toolchains.label: .NET + MAUI
toolchains.about: The .NET SDK plus the maui-android workload: Android apps from C#.

then.note: adding the maui-android workload (android targets from C#)
then.optional: the maui-android workload failed; the plain SDK is still installed

source.online: After the pinned SDK is unpacked, its workload step has dotnet download the maui-android workload's packages from api.nuget.org by itself.

toolchains.name: node
toolchains.label: Node.js
toolchains.about: Node.js and npm, for a project built with npm and for anything that drives a browser with Playwright.

toolchains.name: python
toolchains.label: Python (uv)
toolchains.about: uv and a Python 3.12 with pip and venv, for a project's own dependencies: uv venv, then uv pip install -r requirements.txt. The node's own python3 has neither.

run: dst="$2"; t="$(mktemp -d)"; mkdir -p "$dst/bin" "$dst/libexec"; tar -xzf "$1" -C "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -name uv -type f | head -1)" "$dst/libexec/uv"; chmod +x "$dst/libexec/uv"; rm -rf "$dst/python"; export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$dst/python" UV_CACHE_DIR="$t/cache" UV_NO_CONFIG=1; "$dst/libexec/uv" python install -q 3.12; py="$("$dst/libexec/uv" python find 3.12)"; ln -sf ../libexec/uv "$dst/bin/uv"; ln -sf "$(realpath --relative-to="$dst/bin" "$py")" "$dst/bin/python3.12"; rm -rf "$t"
source.online: uv, its pinned program, downloads the Python 3.12 interpreter from github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone and holds it to the sha256 that release of uv carries for it.

toolchains.name: playwright
toolchains.label: Playwright browsers
toolchains.about: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with the module that drives them, for aerie capture shot and browser tests. Needs node.

run: npm install --prefix "$1" --no-audit --no-fund --loglevel=error playwright@latest && "$1/node_modules/.bin/playwright" install chromium firefox webkit

toolchains.name: lint-tools
toolchains.label: Lint tools (shellcheck, hadolint, actionlint, ruff, yq, fd)
toolchains.about: What aerie lint runs: shellcheck, hadolint, actionlint and ruff, with yq and fd. Without it, aerie lint on a node skips its checks.

run: dst="$2/bin"; t="$(mktemp -d)"; mkdir -p "$dst"; cp "$1" "$dst/hadolint"; get() { curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$2" "$1"; }; tag() { curl -fsSIL -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' "https://github.com/$1/releases/latest" | sed 's#.*/tag/##'; }; get https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_amd64 "$dst/yq"; get https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/releases/latest/download/ruff-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz "$t/ruff.tgz"; tar -xzf "$t/ruff.tgz" -C "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -name ruff -type f | head -1)" "$dst/"; v="$(tag koalaman/shellcheck)"; get "https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/releases/download/$v/shellcheck-$v.linux.x86_64.tar.xz" "$t/sc.txz"; tar -xJf "$t/sc.txz" -C "$t"; cp "$t/shellcheck-$v/shellcheck" "$dst/"; v="$(tag rhysd/actionlint)"; get "https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/releases/download/$v/actionlint_${v#v}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" "$t/al.tgz"; tar -xzf "$t/al.tgz" -C "$t" actionlint; cp "$t/actionlint" "$dst/"; v="$(tag sharkdp/fd)"; get "https://github.com/sharkdp/fd/releases/download/$v/fd-$v-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz" "$t/fd.tgz"; tar -xzf "$t/fd.tgz" -C "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -name fd -type f | head -1)" "$dst/"; chmod +x "$dst"/*; rm -rf "$t"

toolchains.name: ffmpeg
toolchains.label: FFmpeg (video and audio)
toolchains.about: ffmpeg, ffprobe and ffplay, for cutting, converting and sizing video and audio, and for turning a recording into frames a session can look at.

toolchains.name: audio
toolchains.label: Speech in and out (piper, whisper)
toolchains.about: What aerie tool sound say and hear run: piper turns text into speech, and whisper turns a recording back into text with its times. About 800 MB.

credits.name: the ljspeech voice
credits.maker: from Keith Ito's LJ Speech dataset

run:
dst="$2"; mkdir -p "$dst/bin" "$dst/libexec" "$dst/models/voices" "$dst/models/whisper"; rm -rf "$dst"/.work.* 2>/dev/null || true; t="$(mktemp -d "$dst/.work.XXXXXX")"; tar -xzf "$1" -C "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -name uv -type f | head -1)" "$dst/libexec/uv"; chmod +x "$dst/libexec/uv"; rm -rf "$dst/python" "$dst/venv"; export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$dst/python" UV_CACHE_DIR="$t/cache" UV_NO_CONFIG=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1; "$dst/libexec/uv" venv -q --python 3.12 "$dst/venv"; "$dst/libexec/uv" pip install -q --python "$dst/venv/bin/python" piper-tts faster-whisper "av<16"; "$dst/venv/bin/python" -m piper.download_voices --download-dir "$dst/models/voices" en_US-ljspeech-medium; "$dst/venv/bin/python" -c "import sys; from faster_whisper import download_model; download_model('base.en', output_dir=sys.argv[1])" "$dst/models/whisper/base.en"; ln -sf ../venv/bin/piper "$dst/bin/piper"; printf '#!/bin/sh
here="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
exec "$here/../venv/bin/python" "$@"
' > "$dst/bin/python-audio"; chmod +x "$dst/bin/python-audio"; rm -rf "$t" 2>/dev/null || true
verify: import piper, faster_whisper; print('piper and faster-whisper', faster_whisper.__version__)

terms.label: the ljspeech voice, trained on the public-domain LJ Speech dataset

toolchains.name: pytorch
toolchains.label: PyTorch with CUDA (python-ml, numpy, ONNX)
toolchains.about: PyTorch with CUDA, numpy and ONNX, run as python-ml, for training or running a model on the node's NVIDIA card (driver 580 or newer); without a card it runs on the CPU. About 6 GB.

run:
dst="$2"; mkdir -p "$dst/bin" "$dst/libexec"; rm -rf "$dst"/.work.* 2>/dev/null || true; t="$(mktemp -d "$dst/.work.XXXXXX")"; tar -xzf "$1" -C "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -name uv -type f | head -1)" "$dst/libexec/uv"; chmod +x "$dst/libexec/uv"; rm -rf "$dst/python"; export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$dst/python" UV_CACHE_DIR="$t/cache" UV_NO_CONFIG=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy; "$dst/libexec/uv" python install -q 3.12; py="$(find "$dst/python" -path '*/bin/python3.12' -type f | head -1)"; test -x "$py"; "$dst/libexec/uv" pip install -q --python "$py" --break-system-packages torch numpy onnx onnxscript onnxruntime; rel="${py#"$dst"/}"; for n in python-ml torchrun; do if [ "$n" = torchrun ]; then a='-m torch.distributed.run'; else a=''; fi; printf '#!/bin/sh
here="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
exec "$here/../%s" %s "$@"
' "$rel" "$a" > "$dst/bin/$n"; chmod +x "$dst/bin/$n"; done; rm -rf "$t" 2>/dev/null || true
verify: import torch, numpy, onnx; print('torch', torch.__version__, 'cuda', torch.version.cuda)

toolchains.name: graphics
toolchains.label: Graphics tools (ImageMagick, resvg, oxipng, pngquant, cwebp)
toolchains.about: What aerie tool graphics runs: ImageMagick for resizing, cropping and comparing images, resvg for SVG to PNG, and oxipng, pngquant and cwebp for shrinking what an app ships.

run: g="$(ldd --version 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's/.* //')"; case "$g" in [0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;; *) g="";; esac; if [ -n "$g" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n' 2.35 "$g" | sort -V | head -1)" != "2.35" ]; then echo "ImageMagick's AppImage needs glibc 2.35 and this node has $g (Rocky 9 and the other 2.34 systems): the graphics tools cannot run here" >&2; exit 1; fi; dst="$2"; bin="$dst/bin"; t="$(mktemp -d)"; mkdir -p "$bin"; get() { curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$2" "$1"; }; tag() { curl -fsSIL -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' "https://github.com/$1/releases/latest" | sed 's#.*/tag/##'; }; v="$(tag ImageMagick/ImageMagick)"; im="$t/magick.AppImage"; get "https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/releases/download/$v/ImageMagick-$v-gcc-x86_64.AppImage" "$im"; chmod +x "$im"; (cd "$t" && "$im" --appimage-extract >/dev/null); rm -rf "$dst/magick"; mv "$t/squashfs-root" "$dst/magick"; ln -sf ../magick/AppRun "$bin/magick"; rs="$1"; if ! tar -tzf "$rs" >/dev/null 2>&1; then rs="$t/resvg.tgz"; get https://github.com/linebender/resvg/releases/latest/download/resvg-linux-x86_64.tar.gz "$rs"; fi; tar -xzf "$rs" -C "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -name resvg -type f | head -1)" "$bin/"; v="$(tag oxipng/oxipng)"; get "https://github.com/oxipng/oxipng/releases/download/$v/oxipng-${v#v}-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" "$t/ox.tgz"; tar -xzf "$t/ox.tgz" -C "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -name oxipng -type f | head -1)" "$bin/"; get https://pngquant.org/pngquant-linux.tar.bz2 "$t/pq.tbz"; python3 -c 'import sys, tarfile; tarfile.open(sys.argv[1]).extractall(sys.argv[2])' "$t/pq.tbz" "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -name pngquant -type f | head -1)" "$bin/"; wv="$(curl -fsS 'https://api.github.com/repos/webmproject/libwebp/tags?per_page=20' | grep -o '"name": *"v[0-9.]*"' | sed 's/.*"v//; s/"//' | sort -V | tail -1)"; get "https://storage.googleapis.com/downloads.webmproject.org/releases/webp/libwebp-$wv-linux-x86-64.tar.gz" "$t/webp.tgz"; tar -xzf "$t/webp.tgz" -C "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -path '*/bin/cwebp' -type f | head -1)" "$(find "$t" -path '*/bin/dwebp' -type f | head -1)" "$bin/"; chmod +x "$bin"/*; rm -rf "$t"

toolchains.name: diagrams
toolchains.label: Diagram renderers (PlantUML, Mermaid)
toolchains.about: What aerie tool diagrams runs: PlantUML and Mermaid, diagrams drawn from text. Needs jdk and playwright beside it.

run:
dst="$2"; mkdir -p "$dst/bin" "$dst/lib"; cp "$1" "$dst/lib/plantuml.jar"; printf '#!/bin/sh
here="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
exec "${JAVA:-java}" -Djava.awt.headless=true -jar "$here/../lib/plantuml.jar" "$@"
' > "$dst/bin/plantuml"; chmod +x "$dst/bin/plantuml"; npm install --silent --no-audit --no-fund --prefix "$dst" @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli; ln -sf ../node_modules/.bin/mmdc "$dst/bin/mmdc"

toolchains.name: documents
toolchains.label: Document readers (markitdown, PyMuPDF, pandoc)
toolchains.about: What aerie tool docs runs: reads a PDF, Word document, slide deck or spreadsheet as Markdown, draws a PDF's pages as pictures, and converts with pandoc. Also lets Claude Code read PDFs. About 650 MB.

run:
dst="$2"; t="$(mktemp -d)"; mkdir -p "$dst/bin" "$dst/libexec"; get() { curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$2" "$1"; }; tag() { curl -fsSIL -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' "https://github.com/$1/releases/latest" | sed 's#.*/tag/##'; }; tar -xzf "$1" -C "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -name uv -type f | head -1)" "$dst/libexec/uv"; chmod +x "$dst/libexec/uv"; rm -rf "$dst/python" "$dst/venv"; export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$dst/python" UV_CACHE_DIR="$t/cache" UV_NO_CONFIG=1; "$dst/libexec/uv" venv -q --python 3.12 "$dst/venv"; "$dst/libexec/uv" pip install -q --python "$dst/venv/bin/python" 'markitdown[pdf,docx,pptx,xlsx,xls]' pymupdf; ln -sf ../venv/bin/markitdown "$dst/bin/markitdown"; v="$(tag jgm/pandoc)"; get "https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/releases/download/$v/pandoc-$v-linux-amd64.tar.gz" "$t/pandoc.tgz"; tar -xzf "$t/pandoc.tgz" -C "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -path '*/bin/pandoc' -type f | head -1)" "$dst/bin/pandoc"; chmod +x "$dst/bin/pandoc"; test -f "${BB_LIB:-}/poppler.py" || { echo "poppler.py is not beside bb: install this from aerie toolchains" >&2; exit 1; }; cp "$BB_LIB/poppler.py" "$dst/libexec/poppler.py"; for n in pdftoppm pdfinfo; do printf '#!/bin/sh
here="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
exec "$here/../venv/bin/python" "$here/../libexec/poppler.py" %s "$@"
' "$n" > "$dst/bin/$n"; chmod +x "$dst/bin/$n"; done; rm -rf "$t"

toolchains.name: office
toolchains.label: LibreOffice, headless
toolchains.about: What aerie tool office runs: LibreOffice without a window, to turn documents, decks and spreadsheets into PDFs. About 750 MB.

run: dst="$2"; t="$(mktemp -d)"; mkdir -p "$dst/bin"; cp "$1" "$t/lo.AppImage"; chmod +x "$t/lo.AppImage"; (cd "$t" && ./lo.AppImage --appimage-extract >/dev/null); rm -rf "$dst/lo"; mv "$t/squashfs-root" "$dst/lo"; so="$(find "$dst/lo/opt" -maxdepth 3 -path '*/program/soffice' | head -1)"; test -x "$so"; ln -sf "../${so#"$dst"/}" "$dst/bin/soffice"; rm -rf "$t"

toolchains.name: ftp
toolchains.label: File access server (FTPS)
toolchains.about: The server behind a project's File access setting: FTPS on the project's node, where people sign in with their own AerieOS name and password. About 60 MB.

run:
dst="$2"; t="$(mktemp -d)"; mkdir -p "$dst/bin" "$dst/libexec"; tar -xzf "$1" -C "$t"; cp "$(find "$t" -name uv -type f | head -1)" "$dst/libexec/uv"; chmod +x "$dst/libexec/uv"; rm -rf "$dst/python" "$dst/venv"; export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR="$dst/python" UV_CACHE_DIR="$t/cache" UV_NO_CONFIG=1; "$dst/libexec/uv" venv -q --python 3.12 "$dst/venv"; "$dst/libexec/uv" pip install -q --python "$dst/venv/bin/python" pyftpdlib pyopenssl; test -f "${BB_LIB:-}/bbftp.py" || { echo "bbftp.py is not beside bb: install this from aerie toolchains" >&2; exit 1; }; cp "$BB_LIB/bbftp.py" "$dst/libexec/bbftp.py"; printf '#!/bin/sh
here="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
exec "$here/../venv/bin/python" "$here/../libexec/bbftp.py" "$@"
' > "$dst/bin/bb-ftpd"; chmod +x "$dst/bin/bb-ftpd"; rm -rf "$t"

toolchains.name: language-servers
toolchains.label: Language servers (Python, TypeScript)
toolchains.about: Python and TypeScript language servers, so a session sees type errors as it edits rather than at the next build.

toolchains.name: kotlin-lsp
toolchains.label: Kotlin language server
toolchains.about: JetBrains' Kotlin language server, so a session sees Kotlin errors as it edits. Carries its own Java.

run: v="$(sed -n 's#.*"tag_name": *"kotlin-lsp/v\([0-9.]*\)".*#\1#p' "$1" | head -1)"; [ -n "$v" ] || { echo 'no kotlin-lsp release named in the answer' >&2; exit 1; }; a=''; [ "$(uname -m)" = aarch64 ] && a='-aarch64'; t="$(mktemp -d)"; u="https://download.jetbrains.com/language-server/kotlin-server/$v/kotlin-server-$v$a.tar.gz"; curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$t/k.tgz" "$u"; want="$(curl -fsSL --retry 3 "$u.sha256" | cut -d" " -f1)"; got="$(sha256sum "$t/k.tgz" | cut -d" " -f1)"; [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$want" = "$got" ] || { echo "the kotlin server is not what JetBrains says it is (sha256 $got, expected ${want:-none stated})" >&2; exit 1; }; mkdir -p "$2/server" "$2/bin"; tar -xzf "$t/k.tgz" -C "$2/server" --strip-components=1; ln -sfn ../server/bin/intellij-server "$2/bin/kotlin-lsp"; rm -rf "$t"

checksum.why: its address is GitHub's answer naming the release; the server it fetches is checked against JetBrains' .sha256 by its own install command

toolchains.name: rust
toolchains.label: Rust
toolchains.about: rustup, cargo and the stable toolchain. Building for Windows also needs a linker: mingw, or zig with cargo-zigbuild.

after: a Windows target also needs a linker: rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-gnu,
then EXTRA_APT_PACKAGES=gcc-mingw-w64, or aerie toolchains install zig + cargo-zigbuild
source.online: rustup-init, its pinned installer, downloads the stable toolchain from static.rust-lang.org, each file held to the sha256 its channel manifest states.

toolchains.name: swift
toolchains.label: Swift
toolchains.about: The Swift toolchain for Linux: shared logic, server-side Swift, and compiling packages. Not an iOS SDK.

toolchains.name: zig
toolchains.label: Zig
toolchains.about: Zig, and a C and C++ cross-compiler (zig cc) for Windows, macOS and Linux; it also links Rust for those.

toolchains.name: xcodes
toolchains.label: xcodes (Xcode installer)
toolchains.about: Installs and switches Xcode versions on a Mac: run xcodes install --latest on the node, with an Apple ID the first time.
